visual_thesis: A router selects the least costly candidate meeting a correctness threshold, or abstains when none qualifies; workload and version bound the result.
mechanism_metaphor: A faceted request tile enters an open decision fan. A transparent threshold plane separates eligible model specimens from unqualified specimens without invented scores, bars or rankings. Profiled cost tags are plain geometric tags with the exact label Profiled cost, no currency or numeric tokens. The selected eligible path leads to one distinct model output. A clearly separated abstention branch returns control without sending a model call. Place a small held-out-test slice and result-version tab as evidence guides, not causal inputs or guarantees. Two allowed arrowheads: Quality threshold to Lowest eligible cost, conditional on qualification; Quality threshold to Abstain, conditional on no eligible candidate. Never draw both as simultaneous guaranteed outputs. No dashboard, gears, switches, knobs or invented charts.

ARTICLE: Model routing needs a visible quality, cost and abstention policy
Microsoft Research describes Switchcraft, a router that chooses a model using predicted correctness, profiled cost and an abstention option. The project page reports higher evaluated accuracy than the best single candidate at lower cost for its tested model set, but an earlier paper reports different figures. That makes version, workload and decision threshold part of the operating record.
